notes: ROBOTS: https://www.zarahome.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host (HTTP 200, 5,840 bytes). NO Claude agent is named anywhere in it - there is no 'User-agent: ClaudeBot', 'anthropic-ai' or 'Claude-Web' group, and no Content-Signal line. I parsed the file into user-agent groups rather than eyeballing it, because the /itxrest/ question turns on group membership. The result: there are exactly six named-bot groups - HTTrack (Disallow: /), Slurp (Disallow: /), MJ12bot (Disallow: /), proximic (Disallow: /itxrest/*), AmazonProductDiscoverybot (Disallow: /) and AmazonProductBot (Disallow: /) - followed by 'User-agent: *' carrying 247 rules. CONFIRMED MYSELF, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST: 'Disallow: /itxrest/*' appears exactly once in the file, at line 14, and it sits under 'User-agent: proximic' at line 13; the '*' group does not begin until line 20 and contains no /itxrest/ rule at all. We fall under '*', so /itxrest/ is permitted for us. The '*' group disallows checkout/account/wishlist paths, /*search.html*, /*share*, /*shop-the-look*, a list of country stores, secondary-language paths INCLUDING 'Disallow: /fr/en/*' (with only 'Allow: /fr/en$' and '/fr/en/$' for the bare landing page), *hidden/*, *contact-swatches* and a parameter list. TWO CONSEQUENCES I ACTED ON. (1) Because /fr/en/* is disallowed, every URL in this file is the FRENCH /fr/ form; the English FR storefront was never requested. (2) The '*' parameter list at line 309 includes 'Disallow: /*catalogId=*'. That binds us, so unlike the ES pass I did NOT call the storefront menu endpoint /api/storefront/1/stores/<id>/menu?...&catalogId=..., which would have carried that parameter. The tree below therefore comes from the catalogue endpoint alone, whose catalogue id is a PATH segment, not a query parameter. 'celement' is NOT in the disallowed parameter list. No Crawl-delay is declared; probe.py's 2s per-host pacing was left in force throughout. ACCESS - HONEST ACCOUNT: every HTML page on www.zarahome.com is served an Akamai Bot Manager JS interstitial, and I verified this on the FR store myself rather than assuming it from the ES pass. Requesting https://www.zarahome.com/fr/salle-de-bain-miroirs-n2468 with each of the ten curl_cffi fingerprints in probe.PROFILES individually returned, in all ten cases, HTTP 200 with a ~2.26 KB stub containing 'bm-verify', an /interstitial/ iframe and a POST to /_sec/verify - chrome120 2262, chrome124 2256, chrome131 2264, edge101 2262, firefox133 2264, safari15_5 2264, safari17_0 2264, safari17_2_ios 2262, safari18_0 2264, safari18_0_ios 2264 bytes. The r.jina.ai reader prefix returned HTTP 403. I did NOT attempt to solve or circumvent the challenge, and no browser automation was used. That is an ACCESS obstacle and NOT a robots exclusion, and the two are not conflated here. THE RUNG THAT WORKED: the site's own sitemap and catalogue API hosts are not behind the interstitial and are robots-permitted for us. https://www.zarahome.com/8/info/sitemaps/sitemap-index-home-categories-zh.xml returned 200 and lists sitemap-home-categories-zh-fr-0.xml.gz, which contains 664 URLs, every one of them a /fr/ category URL. The /itxrest/ storefront APIs answer plain 200 JSON with no cookie, no session and no challenge. STORE - DISCOVERED FROM THE SITE'S OWN DATA, NOT GUESSED: I walked /itxrest/2/catalog/store/<id> over 84009900-84009919 and read each store's identity document. 84009901 = countryCode 'FR', countryName 'France', storeDefaultLanguageId -2 (French), catalogs[type 1] = {id: 80209919, identifier 'ZH_ONT_SUR_SEASON'}.
